name: Behind-the-Neck Lat Pulldown
instructions: Sit at a lat pulldown station with your thighs secured under the pads and hold the bar with a wide overhand grip.
Lean your torso very slightly forward and keep your head tipped forward.
Pull the bar down behind your head to about ear level, driving your elbows toward the floor.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom, then let the bar rise under control.
Stop immediately if you feel shoulder or neck discomfort.
longevityNotes: Pulling strength balances all the forward-reaching of daily life and protects the shoulders and upper back. A strong back is one of the best predictors of staying active and independent.
overview: A lat pulldown variation that brings the bar behind the head. It demands good shoulder mobility and is not suitable for everyone.

commonMistakes: Pulling the bar below the neck
Leaning back and using body swing
safetyNotes: This variation stresses the shoulder joint; use a light load and skip it if you lack overhead mobility. The front-pulldown is a safer alternative.
